wave_title: Fourteenth generation this cycle. After a genuinely honest negative result (a broad survey for sibling unescaped-join delimiter collisions, independently re-verified), a follow-up broad survey using the cycle's own git history as its exclusion list found this real, previously-unfixed gap in core/src/semantic/function.rs -- a file whose identity_key() formula had been spot-checked earlier this session but whose summary() method, a materially different piece of logic, had never been independently read.
priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity -- highest category in the standing priority order. A direct, named violation of this project's own written contract (SEMANTIC-FACTS.md#functionsignature: 'Must account for parameters/order/types, return type, generics, ABI/calling convention, visibility/export surface, async/coroutine form and language-specific safety/effect qualifiers'), not a style nit -- and the affected field is the SOLE representation of a FunctionSignature claim for any consumer using the compatibility subject/predicate/object envelope instead of the full typed record.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly instructed to build its own exclusion list from this cycle's real commit history (git log) before picking files, avoiding reliance on a possibly-stale list of already-touched files. Its finding was independently re-verified before any change: read the real, current summary() implementation directly, read SEMANTIC-FACTS.md's own FunctionSignature contract text at the cited location, and read runtime/src/census/mod.rs's real compat-fact construction to confirm summary() genuinely is the entire object value (not merely a label alongside other stored attributes, unlike the parallel, already-fixed engineering_graph.rs node-label use).
key_finding: FunctionSignature::summary() read only parameters, return_type, is_async, and is_unsafe -- silently never reading visibility, generics, abi, or is_extern, despite all four being real fields the Rust extractor genuinely populates from syn::Signature (confirmed by this session's own earlier FunctionSignature graph-projection fix, which independently verified the extractor's real population of these exact fields). Concretely: a real `pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn foo<T>(x: T) -> i32` produced a typed record correctly carrying visibility="pub(crate)", is_extern=true, abi=Some("C"), generics=["T"], but summary() rendered only "unsafe fn(x: T) -> i32" -- indistinguishable from a safe-ABI, non-generic, private function to any consumer of the compat SemanticFact.object string. Discovered the bug's severity was even greater than initially reported while implementing the fix: the codebase's OWN pre-existing tests already used visibility: "pub" in their fixtures yet asserted an output string with no "pub" prefix at all -- meaning even the single most common visibility spelling (plain pub) was already silently dropped and this omission had been baked into the test suite as if it were correct, not merely an untested edge case.
verification_before_acting: Read the real, current summary() implementation directly in core/src/semantic/function.rs, confirming exactly which of FunctionSignature's nine fields it reads (four) versus silently ignores (visibility, generics, abi, is_extern).
Read SEMANTIC-FACTS.md's own FunctionSignature section directly, confirming the contract text verbatim rather than trusting the subagent's paraphrase.

Read runtime/src/census/mod.rs's real semantic_observation_fact function directly, confirming object: header.subject.summary() is genuinely the entire object field for the function_signature predicate -- not one of several stored attributes, unlike the already-fixed engineering_graph.rs node-label use (which separately stores is_extern/abi as real graph-node attributes, making its own label incompleteness less severe by comparison, exactly as the survey's report distinguished).

Discovered, while implementing the fix, that both of summary()'s pre-existing tests already set visibility: "pub" in their fixtures yet asserted output strings with no "pub" prefix -- independently confirming the bug's reach into even the most common case, beyond what the initial survey report described.

design_decisions.question: What rendering order and syntax for the newly-added fields?
design_decisions.decision: Match real Rust declaration grammar order (visibility, async, unsafe, extern "abi", fn, generics, params, return type) so the summary remains a faithful source-spelling display, consistent with this method's own documented promise ('A source-spelling display summary... built purely from... source-syntax spelling'). visibility == "inherited" (spelling::visibility_spelling's own name for a private item with no keyword at all) renders as nothing, matching real Rust's own convention of omitting the keyword for private items -- every other value (pub, pub(crate), ...) is a real keyword prefix rendered as-is.

design_decisions.question: Update the two pre-existing summary() tests, or leave them failing?
design_decisions.decision: Updated both to reflect correct behavior: the first (which already used visibility: "pub") now asserts the "pub " prefix is present; the second (previously named/used to demonstrate 'no modifiers when absent' while nonsensically still setting visibility: "pub") had its fixture changed to visibility: "inherited" so it genuinely represents the fully-absent case its own name claims, rather than silently encoding the bug as expected behavior. Added a third, new test exercising the full concrete scenario (pub(crate), unsafe, extern "C", one generic) matching the survey's own reported failure case.

design_decisions.question: A pre-existing runtime test (removing_the_compatibility_fact_projection_would_not_erase_typed_semantic_truth) asserted the compat fact's object string does NOT contain "extern"/"pub" -- a deliberate demonstration of the pre-fix lossiness. How to handle it?
design_decisions.decision: Updated its two now-stale assertions to check for PRESENCE instead of absence (the fix closes exactly the gap this test was built to illustrate), while explicitly preserving and calling out the test's real, deeper, still-valid point via its own untouched facts.clear() mechanism further down: typed_semantic_records is never derived from facts, so the system's correctness never depended on the compat summary's completeness in the first place -- that mechanism, not the string's completeness, is the load-bearing proof, and it required no change.
